_note: Every constant used by analysis/memory_model.py. 1 GB = 1e9 bytes.

model.name: LLaMA-2-7B
model.source: Touvron et al. (2023), Llama 2; released model configuration (hidden_size 4096, intermediate_size 11008, num_hidden_layers 32, num_attention_heads 32, vocab_size 32000)

workloads.source: Comparison workload for Dettmers et al. (2023) Figure 6, which reports batch size 1

bytes_per_param.full_ft_source: Rajbhandari et al. (2020), Sec 3.1: 2 + 2 + 12 = 16 bytes per parameter (mixed-precision Adam)
bytes_per_param.adapter_source: Same accounting as full fine-tuning, applied to trainable adapter parameters only
bytes_per_param.nf4_source: Dettmers et al. (2023), Sec 3: 4-bit NF4; quantization constants 0.5 bits/param, 0.127 bits/param with double quantization (divided by 8 for bytes)
bytes_per_param.nf4_scope: Linear layers inside transformer blocks are quantized; embeddings and output head stay 16-bit (assumption, stated)

activations.recompute_per_layer_bytes: 2*s*b*h, plus one layer of full activations during recomputation
activations.source: Korthikanti et al. (2022), Eq. 1 and Table 2; FlashAttention removes the stored attention-score term because the attention matrix is not materialized (Dao et al., 2022)
activations.lora_note: Applied unchanged to LoRA and QLoRA. Frozen linear layers need not store their inputs, so for LoRA and QLoRA this is an upper bound.
activations.formula_note: Derived for GPT-style blocks; LLaMA uses SwiGLU and RMSNorm, so the per-layer constant is approximate.

logits.source: Assumption: FP32 logits and their gradient, b*s*vocab elements each 4 bytes

cross_checks.source: Dettmers et al. (2023), Appendix G, Figure 6
cross_checks.setting: QLoRA, LLaMA 7B, LoRA on all linear layers (App B.2), batch 1, sequence 512, gradient checkpointing
cross_checks.row_description: QLoRA r64, all linear, double quantization, checkpointing
